metaDescription: How to vet a foundation repair or waterproofing contractor in Ontario, from crack injection to weeping tile and exterior membrane basics to check.
intro: Foundation work ranges from a simple crack injection to a full exterior dig with new weeping tile and membrane, and the right fix depends on where the water is actually getting in. A contractor who diagnoses the cause before quoting a solution is worth more than one who jumps straight to a number.
whatToLookFor: A clear diagnosis of the water entry point before recommending a fix
Experience with both interior crack injection and exterior membrane systems
Knowledge of weeping tile condition and when it needs replacement, not just a sump pump
Proper grading and downspout advice as part of the overall water management plan
A written warranty specific to the crack or area being repaired
typicalCostNotes: Cost varies enormously by scope, a single interior crack injection is a modest, often fixed-fee job, while excavating to replace exterior membrane and weeping tile along a foundation wall is a much larger undertaking, so this is usually quoted per project rather than by a general range. Access, depth of the foundation and whether landscaping or a driveway needs to be removed and restored all factor into the final number.
questionsToAsk: Where do you believe the water is actually entering, and how did you determine that?
Is this a crack injection, an exterior dig, or both, and why?
What is the condition of the existing weeping tile, and does it need replacement?
What warranty applies to this specific crack or wall section?
Will grading or downspouts need to change as part of the fix?
redFlags: Quotes a fix before inspecting the foundation or asking where water appears
Recommends a sump pump alone without addressing failing weeping tile
No written warranty tied to the specific repair location
